cultural.vision_reason: This is a woven Afghan "war rug" depicting a map of Afghanistan, weapons, and military vehicles—a textile craft made in Afghanistan, plausibly by Turkmen weavers (a group known for this rug-weaving tradition), though the piece is misfiled as metalwork rather than textile.

physical.title: rug
physical.summary: Woven Afghan war rug with a cream background, red and green border and white tassels. The main design features a map of Afghanistan in green with rocket launchers and Kalashnikov machine guns depicted inside the map that are pointing at several armoured vehicles and helicopters shown leaving Afghanistan. The rug includes a large poppy plant and a green flag on the right. The lower third of the rug features various types of anti-aircraft guns which are labelled in English script. These include a 12.7mm M1938 DshKM heavy machine gun, known as a 'Dashika' (i.e. 'DASHAKA' on the rug) and a 14.5 ZGU-1 air defence weapon nicknamed 'Zigroat' (i.e. 'ZIGORK' on the rug). Several bands of inscriptions in English and Farsi are spaced around the rug.
